newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER-ZAGALLO SAYS HE IS A BORN WINNER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ZAGALLO SAYS HE IS A BORN WINNER.

text.p: Brazil coach Mario Zagallo, who is hoping to add the Copa America to his personal list of titles, said Tuesday he was a born winner and reiterated his belief in results above all else.
"Performances and declarations are forgotten with time but what are never wiped out are the results," he said.
"I'm a winner," added the veteran coach, who is intensely proud of his record in the game. "I'm a born winner. I was born on the right day. I was born with victory by my side."
Zagallo has won the World Cup twice as a player, once as Brazil coach and once as assistant.
"I'm four-times champion of the world," has become a Zagallo catchphrase and a quick reference to his curriculum vitae is standard reply to any criticism of a Brazil performance under his command.
Brazil face Peru on Thursday in the semifinals of the Copa America, a competition Zagallo has never won as coach and one which Brazil have never won outside their own country.
"We have won all our matches so far without any problems, making the right tactical changes where they had to be made," he said.
Brazil captain Dunga, who will be suspended if he picks up a yellow card against Peru, said the thought of missing the final would not deter him from adopting his usual tough-tackling approach.
"If I have to commit a foul I will do it. The most important thing is that Brazil get to the final," he said.
Dunga complained that Brazil, the only non-Spanish-speaking team in the tournament, were having a tough time with referees. "Because we speak Portuguese we also end up coming off worse," he said.
